description: We are trying to solve certain health problems for astronauts on space missions!
summary:
We developed the Offline Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS), a prototype web-based application that helps astronauts manage medical emergencies in deep space without internet access or real-time support from doctors on Earth.
To solve the Monitoring Health in Space challenge, our system combines three key features: a simple "Input -> Analyze -> Action" symptom checker that delivers instant care steps. A smart digital filter that removes exercise and sweat noise from heart rate sensors. And a high-contrast "Non-Doctor" interface that converts raw vitals into an easy-to-read Green, Yellow, or Red status with visual guides.
This project is important because communication delays in deep space make live medical consultations impossible and time-wasting. Our offline system empowers any crew member to act quickly and stress-free; this protects astronaut health, saves time and helps doctors back on Earth.
details:
We developed the Offline Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS). We developed a prototype website or software app that astronauts can open when there is no internet or Google Cloud access to contact doctors back on Earth. This app uses a simple "Input -> Analyze ->Action" loop:

First, the astronaut selects a symptom from a simple menu(input). Then, the app asks 2 to 3 direct questions to narrow down the issue (analyze). Finally, the system instantly delivers clear, step-by-step care instructions (action plan). We also added Coding Smart Filters for "Signal Noise". During intense exercise, rapid movement and sweat create static that distorts wearable heart sensor readings. Our digital filter cleans messy raw data and outputs a smooth, accurate heartbeat wave. And finally, the Non-Doctor" Medical User. A high-contrast, intuitive interface turns raw biometric data, like heart rate and blood oxygen, into a simple (Green, Yellow, or Red) status, paired with interactive visual guides for immediate care. For coding languages, we used JavaScript, HTML, and C++, and we had some SI help to upgrade our code. We chose the challenge Monitoring Health in space so that these ideas can help doctors monitor and track astronauts in space, and so those ideas also help astronauts monitor themselves and save a lot of time and effort for both parties. So these ideas can actually make a big difference and empower astronauts' health. Our project is creative due to the idea of not using the internet and limiting what astronauts can ask for help in space. And finally, throughout development, our team prioritized system stability, crew reassurance, clear visual data, safety, and efficient time management.
